All thoughts and affections enter into the spheres of Societies with which they agree. Explained.
(This) may be evident from the density of the sphere in which are sensuous Spirits; and from the purity of the sphere in which are Angels.

Around every man, and every good Spirit, there is a general sphere of endeavours from Hell, and a general sphere of endeavours from Heaven. Explained... These are general spheres: there are also particular spheres around every man. Explained... Hence man is in equilibrium...
, Explained.
They go outside the sphere of this solar system...
Outside the sphere where are Spirits of our Earth.

Every Spirit, and still more every Society, is surrounded by a sphere of its own faith and life = a spiritual sphere. By this sphere their quality is known; for it is perceived by those in perception, sometimes at a considerable distance, even when they are hidden, and not communicating by thought or speech.
This spiritual sphere may be compared to the material sphere which encompasses a man's body, which is a sphere of effluvia... and is smelled by keen-scented beasts.
(Thus) if infernals were near those in Divine worship, they would infest them by their sphere; for (the latter) would perceive something abominable.

From what has been said about (this) spiritual sphere... it is evident that there is nothing hidden... of whatever a man had thought, spoken, or done (here); for these are the things which constitute that sphere.
Such a sphere pours from a man's spirit even while he is in the body; and his quality is thereby Known. Illustrated.
While Spirits of Mars occupied the sphere of my mind...
(The Divine truth) may be illustrated by the sphere of charity and faith which proceeds from the Angels...

Every truth has its own extension, which is sometimes manifested by a sphere... The sphere of the extension (there) is to the surrounding Societies. Wherever the sphere extends itself, so far there is communication. (Continued. See
The things a man... entirely believes and loves are perpetually in his thought and will... as is manifest from the spiritual sphere around a Spirit. Explained.
Falsities and evils cannot enter into the sphere where are good and truth. Signified.
The falsities pouring from their evils then constitute a sphere around them, which appears like a dense cloud, or water.
Spheres, called spiritual spheres, continually emane from every Society; they pour out. These spheres are from the activity of their affections and derivative thoughts.
The consociations (there) are all made according to the spheres. Explained.
Each province in the Grand Man has its own distinct sphere...
Hence there is an oppugnancy between the spheres.
In the inmost sphere of Heaven there is a certain progression according to the Divine heavenly form...
Extension into Heaven (only) to the spiritual spheres of good. Signified, Explained.
Every Angel, Spirit, and man has a spiritual sphere, which is according to his extension into Societies... not into the Societies themselves, but into the spheres of their good.
The dominant love constitutes the sphere of everyone's life, and it extends itself according to its quality and quantity.
By the spiritual sphere of good ceasing below. Signified, Explained.
When the sphere of their life does not agree (with the Societies into which they are admitted) conflict ensues...
When a (merely) natural man comes into the spiritual sphere, which is the sphere of life of the internal man, he is insane.
Such are in pain and blindness when elevated into the spiritual sphere.
Their truths ate Known from their faces... and the good itself from them.
Three things with an Angel make a one: his internal... his external... and the sphere of the life of his affections and thoughts, which pours out from him to a distance.
The Divine sphere which proceeds from the Lord, called the Divine truth, is universal, filling the universal Heaven...
A sphere of affections of good and truth is presented before (their) eyes by colours, the specific things by objects variously coloured; and also before the nostrils, by odours.
The power of the Divine sphere. Signified, Explained.

The Divine truth... must be conceived as a sphere from the Sun, decreasing in ardour... as it recedes... Within this sphere, but far from the Sun... is the angelic Heaven. This sphere extends itself also outside of Heaven, even into Hell; but those there... turn it into the contrary.
The sides of the ark
= the Divine sphere encompassing Heaven in its ultimates. Explained.
Through the Divine sphere of good and truth which encompasses and encloses Heaven in general and particular has Heaven been created... and through the same it is conserved...
The termination of the sphere of good from the Divine good. Signified, Explained.

The Divine sphere which encompasses and guards Heaven is a sphere of Divine truth conjoined with Divine good; but the sphere which guards Hell is a sphere of Divine truth separated from Divine good. Explained.
(Thus the former) sphere ceases where Heaven ceases; and (the latter) sphere begins where Hell begins; and in the intervening space there is a conjunction. Signified.
Firmness is in the natural sphere. Signified, Explained.
The conjunction of the one sphere with the other. Signified, Explained.

In Heaven, spheres conjoin; for spheres proceed from every Society, and from every Angel. These spheres exhale from the life of each one's affections of good and truth, and pour themselves out thence to a distance... The Angels and Societies are conjoined, and also disjoined, according to these spheres. Explained.
So far as these spheres derive from the Lord, they conjoin; so far as from an Angel's proprium, they disjoin.
Plenary conjunction in the ultimates of the spheres. Signified, Explained.
Plenary conjunction of one sphere with the other. Signified, Explained.
The sphere of good through which there is conjunction. Signified, Explained.
The power of the sphere of Divine good. Signified, Explained.
Not only Heaven, but all the Societies, and also each Angel... are encompassed with the Divine sphere, which is the good and truth proceeding from the Lord...
The sphere of Divine good through which there is conjunction from the higher part of Heaven. Signified, Explained.
The conjunction of the sphere of Divine good in the extremes of Heaven. Signified, Explained.
The conjunction and conservation of all things of Heaven through the sphere of Divine good in the externals of the Spiritual Kingdom. Signified, Explained.
What is perpetual and impressed on hearts according to the heavenly sphere. Signified, Explained.

The love constitutes the whole man there, and the derivative sphere of life flows forth from him like an exhalation or vapour, and encompasses him, and makes as it were himself around him... like the effluvium around plants... and beasts... Such an effluvium pours out of every man... But (after death) this effluvium... is not material... but is a spiritual effluence from his love, which forms a sphere around him...
As this sphere is communicated to others, and is transferred into them... and is received by them according to their love, it gives rise to many wonderful things there. Enumerated.
From the spheres of their affections... their quality as to love is perceived.
For evils cannot endure the sphere of good. Described, Signified.
The sphere of Divine good through which there is conjunction and conservation. Signified, Explained.
The sphere of Divine good infils universal Heaven, and extends itself into Hell; for it is like the sphere of the sun's heat...
This Divine sphere has been likened to radiant circles...
They who suffer themselves to be led by the Lord... are in the sphere of Divine good... (others) are in the same sphere, but their interiors are closed so that they do not feel the influx...
Hence the external sphere of Divine good is dulled in Hell, yet the internal sphere remains, which is not received... but still the Lord rules the Hells through it.
The reason why there is a sphere of Divine good. Explained.

Moreover, from every Angel proceeds a sphere from his love; and also from every good or evil Spirit, according to their loves; but the spheres proceeding from these do not extend themselves far; but the Divine sphere into the universe; for it proceeds from the inmost, which is the all in all the successives.
Concerning these spheres. References.

Thus the Divine sphere round about is a sphere of the good of love from the Lord as a Sun from the east even to the west, and a sphere of truth from good from the south to the north. Thus the sphere of Divine good in the midst is like an axis, and the sphere of Divine truth thence proceeding is on both sides. Signified.
Anxiety was felt, arising from a collision of the spheres. Explained.
Spiritual spheres of life proceed from every Angel and Spirit... by which their quality is known. Explained.
The spheres which go forth from the Angels are so full of love that...
All the Societies communicate by an extension of the spheres.
The sphere of the life is a sphere of the affections which are of love and faith. This extends itself into the Societies. Described.
[Swedenborg footnote 1.]. A spiritual sphere, which is a sphere of the life, flows forth from every man. Spirit, and Angel. References.
The things above the sphere of nature.
When elevated into the interior sphere of Heaven.
The sphere exhaled from Hell is like a perpetual endeavour to dissolve and violate marriages.
When good Spirits perceive this delight... from the sphere of an Angel's love... they come into a sweet swoon.
(Spirits recognise others) by the sphere of their life, when they approach.
The sphere of falsity from evil flowing from Hell. Described.
From Heaven was perceived a sphere of truth from good bridling (it). Hence an equilibrium.
This sphere from Heaven was perceived to be from the Lord alone, although it appeared to be from the Angels. Explained.
From each Hell is exhaled a sphere of the cupidities in which are those there. When this sphere is perceived by one in like cupidity... he is filled with delight. Explained.

A spiritual sphere encompasses everyone, which pours forth from the life of the affections and derivative thoughts... Hence such a sphere of life flows forth from every Heavenly Society, and from every infernal one, consequently from all of them together, that is, from the whole Heaven, and the whole Hell. (The equilibrium thence resulting. Explained.)
The sphere flowing from the Hells is wholly a sphere of endeavours to destroy the Divine of the Lord...
The Divine sphere proceeding from the Lord is a perpetual endeavour to save all...
The Divine external sphere of the Word. Signified.
The sphere of the Word from the Lord's Divine good and truth. Signified.

The spiritual Sun is like the sphere... which encompasses each Angel, whereby his presence is presented... and which is not the Angel himself, but is from each and all things of his body, from which substances continually emane in a stream... These substances... excite the atmospheres... and thus present a perception as of his presence...
Thus it is not a different sphere of affections and derivative thoughts... which goes forth and is continued...
There is such a sphere around every Angel, because there is one around the Lord; and that sphere around the Lord is in like manner from Him, and is their Sun.

(The spheres around Angels and Spirits, and the general spheres around Societies, I have seen as thin flame, gross fire, bright cloud, and black cloud; and I have perceived these spheres as odours) by which I have been confirmed that a sphere consisting of substances set free from their bodies encompasses everyone in Heaven and in Hell.

A sphere pours forth (also) from every thing in the Spiritual World. Enumerated. It is similar in the natural world. Explained. The natural world derives this from the Spiritual World, and the Spiritual World from the Divine.

(Natural substances and matters) have brought [with them] by continuation from the substance of the spiritual Sun... the sphere which encompasses the Lord; (and) from this sphere, by continuation from the Sun... have originated the substances and matters from which are earths.
The delight of these affections... encompasses everyone there as his atmosphere; and all are conjoined according to these spheres exhaled from their affections through their thoughts...

The Divine sphere which encompasses the Lord is from His Divine love and Divine wisdom simultaneously; and is represented in the Celestial Kingdom as rubescent... in the Spiritual as cerulescent... and in the Natural as viridescent...
(In the second kind of enchantment) the spiritual sphere of their mind dispelled the spiritual sphere of the other's mind, and suffocated it.
The virgins perceive from their sphere, etc. their quality as to the love of the sex.

A universal conjugial sphere proceeds from the Lord, and pervades the universe... The reason such a sphere of the marriage of good and truth proceeds from Him, is that it is also a sphere of propagation... and this is the same as the Divine Providence for the conservation of the universe...
, General article.

As this universal sphere... inflows into its subjects according to their form... the male receives it... in the understanding, and the female... in the will... and, as this sphere is also a sphere of prolification, it follows that thence is the love of the sex.
That a sphere of lasciviousness pours out from the unchaste, is evident from the Israelitish statutes...
A wife is conjoined with her husband through the sphere of her life which goes forth from her love.
From every man there pours out a spiritual sphere... which applies itself to the natural sphere which is from the body, and they conjoin themselves.
A natural sphere continually flows out from the body... from man, beasts, trees, fruits, flowers, and metals... So in the Spiritual World; but the spheres... there are spiritual...

The spheres which emane from Spirits and Angels are inwardly spiritual, because the affections... and derivative interior perceptions and thoughts are in them. This is the source of all sympathy and antipathy, and of all conjunction and disjunction; and presence and absence there are according to them... and therefore these spheres cause the distances there.

What these spiritual spheres operate in the natural world is known to some. The inclinations of married partners towards each other are from this origin. Unanimous and concordant spheres unite them; and adverse and discordant ones disunite them...
Every part both within and without man renovates itself... and thence is the sphere...
This sphere encompasses a man... thinly on his back, and densely on his breast; and the latter conjoins itself with his respiration. (The effect of this on consorts.)
The spheres which go forth from every part of a man, and which are continued amply around him, conjoin or disjoin consorts not only from without, but also from within...
The sphere of love going forth from a wife who is tenderly loved, is perceived in Heaven as sweetly fragrant...
Many spheres proceed from Him. Enumerated... But the universal of them all is the conjugial sphere. Explained.
This conjugial sphere infills the universe, and pervades it from primes to ultimates. Explained.
This sphere is more universal than the sphere of (natural) heat and light. Explained.
This sphere is received by the female sex, and through it is transferred into the male. Explained.
Where there is love truly conjugial, this sphere is received by the wife, and by the husband through her alone. Explained. (This is the test of this love.
Where there is love not conjugial, this sphere is received by the wife, but not by the husband through her. Explained.

This conjugial sphere... is Divine in its origin; in its progress into Heaven... is celestial and spiritual; with men is natural; with beasts and birds animal; with worms merely corporeal; and with plants is devoid of life. Moreover it is varied in each subject according to its form.

As this sphere is received immediately by the female sex, and mediately by the male, and is received according to the forms, it follows that this sphere, which is holy in its origin, can, in the subjects, be... turned into the opposite. The sphere opposite to it is called meretricious with such women, and scortatory with such men; and, as these are in Hell, this sphere is thence. But this sphere, also, is of much variety... and every man attracts such a species of it as is in congruity with himself...
Thus a man who does not love his wife, receives this sphere from some other source... yet this also is inspired by her...
This propagative or plastic force in seeds... and in souls... is from the conjugial sphere...

The sphere of love from the wife, and the sphere of understanding from the husband, constantly flows forth; and this [sphere] perfects the conjunctions, is around them with its pleasantness and breathing, and unites them.

For a universal sphere of generating and propagating the celestial things of love, the spiritual things of wisdom, and the derivative natural things of offsprings, proceeds from the Lord, and infils the universal Heaven and the universal world; and this heavenly sphere infills the souls of all mankind, and descends through their minds into their bodies down to the ultimates, and gives the force of generating... with those who suffer themselves to be restored to the primeval state.
Two universal spheres proceed from the Lord to conserve the universe... a sphere of procreating, and a sphere of protecting the things procreated.
The proceeding Divine is called a sphere, because...

All that which flows forth from a subject, and encompasses and environs it, is called a sphere; as the sphere of light and heat around the sun; the sphere of life from a man; the sphere of odour from a shrub; the sphere of attraction from the magnet.

The universal spheres here treated of are from the Lord around Him, and proceed from the (spiritual) Sun. (Thus) proceeds a sphere of heat and light, (that is), a sphere of love and wisdom, to operate ends which are uses. This sphere is distinguished by various names, according to the uses. Enumerated.
These two universal spheres make a one with the sphere of conjugial love and the sphere of the love of infants. Explained.
These two spheres inflow universally and singularly into all things of Heaven and of the world, from primes to ultimates. Explained.
The sphere of the love of infants. Explained.
This sphere affects both the evil and the good. Explained.
This sphere affects, principally, the female sex... Explained.
This sphere is also a sphere of innocence and peace. Explained.
The sphere of innocence inflows into infants, and through them into the parents. Explained.
It also inflows into the souls of the parents, and conjoins itself with the same sphere in the infants... (Explained.)
The sphere of the love of procreating progresses in order... Explained.
There is a sphere of scortatory love, and a sphere of conjugial love. Explained.
, Explained.
These two spheres meet each other in both worlds; but do not conjoin themselves. Explained.
Between these two spheres there is equilibrium; and man is in it. Explained.
Each sphere bears delights with it. Explained.
The sphere of the lust of fornicating... is intermediate between the sphere of scortatory and the sphere of conjugial love, and makes an equilibrium. Explained.
His Sun... consists of the Divine essence, which goes out as a sphere from Him.
The Divine love is Known from its sphere, which pervades the universe...
This universal sphere affects... those who receive this love of God...
The same Divine sphere operates into inanimate things... but through the (natural) sun...
His omnipotence operates within the sphere of the extension of good, which sphere is infinite; for this sphere infils the universe from the inmost. (Its operation explained.)
There continually proceeds from the Lord a Divine celestial sphere towards all who embrace the doctrine of His Church, and obey Him... and want to be instructed by Him.
From this celestial sphere arises a natural sphere, which is one of love towards children; which sphere is most universal, affecting (both animate and inanimate things). Explained.
From the influx of that celestial sphere into the natural world come forth (the wonders of plant life, and the singing of birds). Explained.

The reason evil and good cannot be together... is that in the Spiritual World there exhales from everyone the sphere of his love, which... causes sympathies and antipathies. By these spheres the good are separated from the evil.

The affections and thoughts there make a spiritual sphere around them, which is felt in various ways. But (here) this spiritual sphere is absorbed by the material body; and it encloses itself within the natural sphere, which then pours out of the man.
The spiritual sphere which reigned in those feasts (of charity) was a sphere of love to the Lord and of love towards the neighbour. (Its effects on them.)
For there emanes from every man a spiritual sphere... which interiorly affects his associates, especially at feasts; it emanes through the face and respiration.

(Metals, etc.) absorb the ether, breathe out their native [qualities], reject the obsolete things, and redintegrate themselves with new ones; and hence there is a magnetic sphere round the magnet, an irony one round iron, a coppery one round copper, a silvern one round silver, a golden one round gold, a stony one round stone, a nitrous one round nitre, a sulphurous one round sulphur, and a various one round each particle of... earth from which the inmost of seeds are impregnated. Explained.
If you could feel the sphere of life pouring from everyone's native disposition...
(Effect of) the spheres (there) which flow forth from modern Christianism...
One sphere... takes away faith in the Divine of the Lord's Human. Explained.
A second sphere, which takes away faith, is like a black cloud in winter. Explained.

A third sphere is that of the conjunction of faith and charity, which is so strong that it cannot be resisted; but at this day is abominable. Explained. This sphere invades men (here) also, and extinguishes the conjugial torches between truths and goods. Described.
The Angels complain of these spheres, and pray to the Lord to dissipate them; but... they cannot be dissipated so long as the dragon is
on the earth
These three spheres are like tempest-driven atmospheres... and, being spiritual, they invade minds and drive them.
The spheres of spiritual truths there are as yet few... which is the reason why those Truths are so inconspicuous with men...

There is a sphere elevating all to Heaven which continually proceeds from the Lord, and infils the universal spiritual and natural worlds; it is like a strong current... which secretly carries along a ship. All who believe in the Lord and live according to His precepts enter this sphere or current... But they who do not believe, do not want to enter it...
See
On the general sphere of Spirits (before the Last Judgment). Explained.
The sphere of Spirits is now so perverted...
How this general sphere operates into human minds.

(This) general life... diffuses itself, and constitutes a sphere, which is called the sphere of activity, and [extends] itself into the more subtle things of nature. Every Genius and Spirit has his own sphere of activity... so, therefore, have all of them together...
On the general spheres... from the things of God Messiah's Kingdom. Explained.
The rational sphere.
There are also spheres of evil Spirits, (which) fire turned into infernal ones at the Last Judgment. Described.
On the more interior sphere. Described.
Tranquil spheres, to be called spheres of ignorance. Explained.
There is a certain sphere exhaling not concordant with my thought. Explained.
On spheres of activity of Spirits and Angels. General article.
A sphere of spiritual effluvia (from Spirits).
On a circumfused spiritual sphere, and its operation into Spirits. Explained.
A number of Spirits, or Societies, together form a general sphere. Example(s).
That activities of sphere encompass men. Explained.
There is not the smallest particle which has not its own sphere around it; and the conformable parts constitute a general sphere conformable to the parts.
There are spheres of all things...
The sphere of the Lord...
On the sphere of hearing. Explained.
On the spheres of Spirits. Explained.
(The amending of a person's sphere.)
There can be no particular without a general... Thus it is the general sphere which affects... Alan cannot speak, etc., unless there be a certain universal sphere of thoughts. Explained.
, Explained.
Whence are the spheres which rule the thoughts.
There are indefinite varieties of general spheres...
The spheres proper to Angels, etc., are not mixed with the Lord's spheres...

(There is a sphere of Spirits round man, he being like a solid point in the middle of it, just in the same way as the terracqueous globes are surrounded by their atmospheric spheres. But when the corporeal things are laid aside, man is in that sphere in the same way as is a Spirit.) Further described.

In the atmospheric sphere, incongruous things are dispelled, and so the sphere by its own forces reduces all things to equilibrium. Example(s). Spiritual spheres are the cause of this. (Example of a spiritual sphere being purged in the same way.)
There are spheres which have limits, which Spirits cannot pass. Explained.
The sphere of their activity does not extend far: but ceases at once at a small circumference. Explained.
Deceits occupy this interior sphere...
Insanity reigns in the interior sphere of the World of Spirits. General article.
In the interior sphere of upright Spirits.
All the genera and species of Spirits have their own spheres, into which only like ones can enter. Explained.
All are distinguished not only according to such exterior spheres, but also according to their interior ones...
A bloody sphere. Described.
, Explained.
In order that a man or Spirit may be in an Angelic sphere, it is necessary that...
On the sphere of those who are worldly (there), and desire to command others. (Its potent effects on others).

Within the sphere of the speech, that is, in the sphere of the thoughts within the speech, in which are interior Spirits... They can transmit themselves into that interior sphere, and this get out of the society of those in the exterior sphere.
On the speech of the Spirits of the interior sphere.
In the interior sphere of nature are thousands of such as are evil... as to the interiors of nature.
In the interior sphere are the ends which cease in the world and self...
On a sphere of persuasions of evil exercised by some Spirits, Explained.
Thus the sphere of a certain love conjoins chickens with their mother.
Persuasion forms a sphere, into which evil Spirits cannot enter. Example(s).
On general spheres. General article.
The four spheres of faith, enumerated. The opposite spheres are also four.
One general sphere contains other general spheres. Explained.
, Explained.
One sphere also succeeds another.
Of the Spirits in one place, each can he in a different sphere...
The corporeal sphere. Explained.
On the sphere of activity of infants.
Spheres... are presented by odours. Explained.
Spheres of terror, sadness, etc.
Evil Spirits cannot bear a sphere of faith; and therefore the perception of spheres is taken away, diminished, or increased by the Lord...
When they want to explore the angelic sphere... it so penetrates into the interiors of the Spirit that he is turned into such things...
Certain Spirits, or Societies, cannot live in the next purer sphere. Explained.
On spheres. General article.
The only sphere Known to man is odour...
Another sphere known to man, is that he desires this or that food...
But in the other life there are spiritual spheres so perceptible that...
Such spheres are innumerable, being as many as there are Spirits, and Societies.
A general mixed sphere of a number of Spirits is at once discriminated by the Angels...
There is a perceptible sphere of every phantasy; and while a Spirit is mute, and hardly thinks at all, it is perceived by others. They are not aware that they have such a sphere...
When I was extracting what I had written about spheres, not being in perception from a sphere, I did not know what a sphere is, neither did the Spirits around me...

Animals sensate from spheres what they would never perceive in any other way; so that there are spheres in the nature of Things which are quite unknown to man, but which reign with beasts. Thus a dog... Knows his master among a thousand from a sphere of subordination and of friendship... This is ascribed to effluvia...
Animals have a sphere of knowing the quarters of the world...
Animals have also a sphere of gladness...
All animals have spheres of knowing what to eat...
Animals have a sphere of times: as swallows, etc.
Birds have a sphere of building their nests... They have a sphere of bringing up their young.

Such (corporeal and natural) spheres reign with animals; but do not exist with man, because he is in phantasies, (otherwise) he would have these lowest spheres, and also a sphere of Knowing his associate the moment he saw him, that is, his quality...
As to the sphere of faith, he would Know their quality as to faith, like a Spirit, at their first coming... These spheres are human.

Such spheres are of the Lord alone; for they descend from the sphere of faith in Him; from and through this, all the other spheres are distinguished, and they flow forth from it; and therefore spheres of odour correspond...
There are also visual spheres, distinct from those spheres which are of odour; (as) a sphere of grace (visible) as a golden yellow atmosphere...
A sphere seen as of mere human flesh. (It was) one of human affection; thus truly human.

Angels do not know they are in a sphere of the perception of faith, unless the Lord grants them to perceive it, (This is) because they are in it, (just as) gardeners do not perceive the sphere of the odour of flowers...
The odours of those in outermost things... are spheres flowing forth from them. Example(s).
On a sphere of persuasion.
By his phantasies he perverted the spheres.
(The extraordinary sphere of Dippel.) Described.
They perceived my previous quality from my sphere.
On the general sphere of those who suppose Spirits to be like the atmosphere. Described.
One infant, or Angel, can drive away myriads of Spirits; for they cannot endure the sphere of mutual love...
Man's interior man is in this sphere.
The evil who are in the interior sphere...
(His sufferings) when he came into the sphere of angelic Spirits.
The bodily fluids have not their up and down according to the sphere outside the body...
A sphere of abominable adultery exhaled from them.
When I smelled the dung of horses, upright Spirits complained... because there at once occurred a sphere of reasonings from natural things...

Thus... the objects of odours and of the other senses, and also the objects of various thoughts, as also phantasies, all form spheres, to which correspond spiritual and celestial things, consequently their spheres which affect Spirits according to their quality; for spheres are as it weie the atmospheres in which Spirits live.
Evil Spirits want to throw me under the wheels of carriages... the sphere of their endeavour is constantly such...

When I ate butter, certain Spirits... could not bear it, because... it gave rise to a sphere of goods... So (tea pleased them) solely because they derived thence a sphere of there being what is less spiritual. So with many other things I ate and drank...
How the evil in the interior sphere are infested and tortured.
The state of the happy in the interior sphere.
So also various and manifold spheres are formed from Things; as various spheres of goodness...
A sphere was represented as an aura of uses... In such a sphere he began to flee.

Every Spirit, and still more every Society, exhales a sphere of itself, which is from its life of principles; (with) evil Genii, from the life of cupidities. Hence their sphere, which is a sphere as it were of derivative instincts. This sphere is a certain General operating, and when it acts into the memory of a man, it excites thence whatever is accordant... When such a sphere reigns, all things which are excited, however false, appear as true, and confirm...
, Explained.
(Various visible spheres. Described.)
The quality of the spheres of Spirits which arise from dissent, or consent... Explained.
Such a force of persuading is a general sphere...
When such spheres were shown me by colours...
The great density of the sphere which has to be dissipated...
A sphere of good and truth which cannot yet penetrate through the sphere of persuasions. Representation.
The amount of the sphere may thus be observed.
Round everyone in falsity and evil there are such dense spheres...

These spheres appear as in clear day to good Spirits and Angels, whose spheres cannot possibly accord... and therefore they are dissociated. If they come together, those who have a sphere of falsity and evil around them are greatly tortured; and if, by permission, the spheres of falsity and evil prevail, the good come into temptation, anxieties, and anguish. The respiration is as it were taken away, so that one cannot live in the sphere of the other unless they are miraculously tempered.

There is a spiritual sphere around everyone, as there is a natural sphere, and also a corporeal one. That everyone has this latter, may be evident from the effluvious expiration, which is like a sea around a man.
Hence comes that sphere of self-honour.
How men acquire spheres.
, Explained.
Such spheres are things which are manifestly perceived (there). Explained.
Such spheres are wont to be turned into spheres of odour...
They are also wont to be turned into visible spheres, and appear as forms of a sphere...
Their sphere is continually of adulteries... Their sphere is turned into an intestinal sphere...
Hence come spheres of faith.
Spheres are such that they affect all who are like them. Example(s).
On spheres of affection.
Certain Societies... were affected by a sphere of the Lord's affections... while other Societies, in the same sphere, could not (be).
Every sphere of affection is attended with there being a certain General...

Very many Spirits transfer themselves into a more subtle sphere... and, when they come into it, it is their interiors which operate... Unless a Spirit is amended before he comes thither, his evil is continued there... and therefore Spirits who are being vastated are not permitted to come into that second sphere until they have been vastated... A woman often appeared to Aristotle, who stroked his cheek with her beautiful hand. Such women were sometimes seen by the ancients, who called them Pallases, and the one who appeared to him was from the Spirits who as men in ancient times had been delighted with ideas...

It might be supposed that the spirit dwells within the body, and that the body as it were clothes it; but it is to be known that the spirit of man is in the body, in the whole, and in every part of it; and that it is its purer substance, in both its motory and its sensory organs, and everywhere else; and that the body is what is material everywhere annexed to it... This is what is meant by man being a Spirit, and the body serving him for uses in the world; and by the spirit being the internal of man, and the body his external. From this it is evident that after death man is in similar active and sensitive life: and is also in the human form, as (here), but in a more perfect one.

For the internal man, or spirit of man, knows not what old age is; but, as the body, or external man, grows old, the former passes into newness of life: the spirit of man is perfected in age as his Corporeal decreases, and still more so in the other life...

Although the spirit knows not what old age is, (and) the spirit is what thinks in the body, and the body has life from it; (yet) this thought of the spirit cannot be communicated to the body, and so cause man to know that he lives after death, for the reason that so long as the spirit remains in the body, it cannot think otherwise than from the principles which the natural man has imbued...

Explained... That I might be certain of these things, it has been granted; me to touch Spirits themselves, and to speak with them often about this subject.
, Explained.

I have sometimes thought and spoken without reflecting that Spirits were present; but they at once addressed me, and told me that they did not know it was not they who were thinking. The nearest Spirits believed it was themselves altogether; the more remote ones less so; and those still more remote, still less so.

Spirits have long been with me, neither very good, nor very evil, who could inflow inwardly into the affections... and they so bound themselves to me that it seemed as if they could scarcely be separated. Described. (This shows that it is loves which conjoin.)

Spirits are associated to a man according to his loves... As soon as I have begun to love anything intensely, Spirits were present who were in such love, and they were not removed until the love had ceased.

When I have thought about a man known to me... that whole man, as he existed in my thought and affection, appeared in a moment with the Spirits. So when I have thought of any city... the Spirits knew in a moment everything I had seen or known about it. It is the same with matters of knowledge. (Explained.)

Thus did my thought appear with Spirits when I was a little withdrawn from sensuous things; but (not) when my thought was in sensuous things... To the sensuous are adjoined like Spirits; and these Spirits apprehend scarcely any more things with a man than those which come to his sensation; for they are grosser than the rest.

When I have been let down into what is sensuous... the Spirits who are in that grosser sphere infused shocking and scandalous things... At this day such Spirits abound... and the influx from them with man causes him to be self-indulgent, and live for himself and the world... To be elevated from them, man must think about eternal life.

When Spirits have inquired anything from me, they have received an answer by merely looking into my thought.

The reason was that they had placed life in the body. Explained... But the unlearned, who have been in the good of faith, are not such...

Through changes of state, Angels and Spirits can be translated from one place to another; from one Earth into another; and even to Earths at the end of the universe. In like manner a man as to his spirit...
Spirits who are in the First Heaven.
There are always Spirits and Angels with man... Through them man is connected with the Lord; and thus subsists the human race and also Heaven.
The Spirits of (the First Earth).
, General article.
For Spirits remain near their own Earth.
, Explained.
In that gulf appeared very many men, who were Spirits... These were guards, to prevent Spirits from this system from passing, without permission, into any other.

in the Word, = the life of the intellectual part;
heart,

. Illustrated.
Filled with the spirit of wisdom
) = with Divine truth. Explained.

often occurs in the Word, and, when man is treated of, by his
spirit
is signified the good and truth inscribed on the intellectual part, consequently, the life of this; (for) man, as to his interiors, is a Spirit, and as to them is together with Spirits.
, Explained, Illustrated.
Hence by
Spirit,
when the Lord is treated of, is meant the Divine truth proceeding from His Divine good; and this, when... received by man, is
the Spirit of Truth,
the Spirit of God,
and

, Illustrated.
That
spirit,
in a general sense, = the life of man's respiration. Illustrated.
Thus
spirit
= the life of man. That, in special, it = the life of truth, which is the life of the intellectual part, and is called intelligence. Illustrated.
The Spirit,
here, = intelligence and wisdom.
The life from Divine truths is
Spirit.
The Divine truth, consequently the Divine wisdom and intelligence, are called
the Spirit of Jehovah;
here,
the spirit of wisdom and intelligence, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Jehovah

That
the Spirit of Jehovah
= the Divine truth, and the derivative heavenly life for the man who receives it. Illustrated.
Spirit of judgment
= Divine truth. ( = wisdom from Divine truth.
Spirit of holiness
= the Lord as to Divine truth, thus the Divine truth which is from the Lord.
To
make angels spirits
) = receptions of Divine truth.
When intelligence and wisdom are taken away from Spirits, which happens when the angelic Societies are removed from them, their head covering appears to be taken away, and they then become stupid...
All Spirits and Angels appear clothed in garments according to their state of truth.
The breath of the nostrils
= the heavenly life itself which is from the Lord.
The Spirits of the Second Earth. General article.
The breath of His mouth
) = the life from Divine truth.
The spirit breatheth where it listeth, and thou hearest the voice thereof, but knowest not whence it Cometh and whither it goeth; so is everyone who is born of the spirit
the spirit
= the life of charity through faith. ( = the Divine truth which inflows from the Lord through the internal of man into his externa, whence the regenerating man has the life of faith.

(The spirit is not continuous with the body.)
Around Spirits who are in truths from good appear most beautiful representatives. Described... But around those in truths (only), appear rocks, marshes, etc.
Unless Spirits and Angels were with man, through whom the influx is effected, he could not live a moment...
With Spirits below the Heavens, there are riches according to their reception of truth and good from the Lord.
Spirits and Angels think by spiritual ideas, and also speak by them...
Spirit
is opposed to
flesh,
because by
Spirit
is signified life from the Lord; and by
flesh,
life from man. Illustrated.
Among Spirits are very many who imitate Divine things...
Spirits are nothing but their own truths and goods which they had put on in the world; and yet are human forms...
The Spirits of the Third Earth, Described.
They could not be with the Spirits of our Earth.
. Explained.
, Explained.
For Spirits are consociated and dissociated according to the affections and the derivative thoughts.
Therefore the Spirits of that Earth do not appear in a well-defined human form; but as clouds. Described.
I have filled him with the spirit of God
) = influx and illustration from the Divine truth which is from the Lord's good.
These Spirits keep themselves at a distance, because their correspondence is... with man's interior things.
(I told him) that what he reprehended was not mine, but belonged to the Spirits around me; for what I think I do not think from myself, but from them, by influx.
As there is nothing Divine in them, it is said
there is no breath in them
Spirits turn themselves according to their loves. Explained.

Spirits go nowhere else than to those with whom they are consociated by love; hence the quality of Spirits as to truth is known from the ways and streets in which they go; for all truth leads to its own love.
The Spirits of the Fourth Earth. Described.
I was not conveyed to the Fourth Earth; but the Spirits of it were brought to me.
How Spirits of quite another genius may be associated with Spirits with whom there is to be conjunction. Explained.

The External (of man) which is accommodated to uses in the other life together with the internal (of man) is called a Spirit; a good Spirit and Angel if the man had been good; and an evil Spirit if he had been evil.
The spirit of man appears (there) in a human form exactly as (here). (His faculties enumerated.)
These ideas are of man's spirit... and he comes into them when he becomes a Spirit, and by them converses with other Spirits.
Those who think in their spirit abstractedly from their body...
As to his spirit, man is in society with Spirits, and, as to his interior thought... with Angels. Hence man has the faculty of thinking.
Angels and Spirits... have faces, arms, hands, feet... dwellings; and live together exactly as do men, upon an earth. Described.
A Spirit with me who had been a very pathetic preacher. Described.
The Spirits of the Fifth Earth. Described.
Spirits from our Earth visit them. Described.
All Spirits know about their own Earth, when their natural memory is opened...

The Spirits said that when leave is given they appear to the inhabitants of their Earth, and speak with them as men; which is effected by their being let into their natural memory... and the inhabitants suppose them to be men (until) they vanish. Illustrated. This rarely happens now on our Earth, lest men should be compelled to believe...
The preacher took hold of the hand of a woman on that Earth; but, as she perceived that he was a Spirit... she hastened away.

Every man is a Spirit as to his interiors, and it is that which lives in the body... and it is the spirit of everyone from which he has the human form, consequently which is principally the man, and in a like form... visible (only) before the eyes of Spirits...
On my asking Spirits... whether they wanted to be reclothed with their earthly body, they fled far away...
Many Spirits and Angels from our Earth accompanied me (to the Sixth Earth).
Only in two places (on the way) did I see Spirits...
The Spirits of the Sixth Earth. Described.
, General article.
The spiritual Sun appears only to the Angels, and not to the Spirits who are below. Explained.
Monkish Spirits seen with a crowd of Spirits of the Sixth Earth, mostly evil. Described.
For Spirits and Angels dwell in the same way as they had done (here). Explained.
Spirits and Angels... can see the things in the world through the eyes of a man to whom the Lord grants to speak with Spirits and Angels...
Upright Spirits... grieved at the ignorance within the Church about Spirits and Angels; and indignantly told me to relate that they are not minds without form, nor ethereal spirits

The pulmonary breath = the understanding, and the truth of faith.

The spirit... in some who were beautiful in face (was seen to be) deformed, black, and monstrous... But in some who were not beautiful, it was lovely, fair, and angelic. And the spirit of a man appears after death such as it had been in the body.
The interiors make the face of an Angel and a Spirit.
Man, too, as to his spirit, turns in the same way. Explained.
A Spirit who believed that he thought from himself. Described.

When an Angel or Spirit comes to a man, and, by conversion to him, is conjoined with him, he comes into all his memory, insomuch that he scarcely knows but that he knows from himself all the man knows...
At this day there is no longer such conjunction with Angels, but with Spirits not in Heaven.
Spirits will not believe it is the man who speaks, but they in him; (and) that all the man knows is from them...

Another reason why Angels and Spirits conjoin themselves so closely with man that they suppose the man's things to be their own, is that there is such a conjunction between the spiritual and the natural world with man that they are as it were one. But, as man had separated himself from Heaven, it was provided... that there should be Angels and Spirits with every man, and that he should be ruled by the Lord through them. This is the reason for so close a conjunction. Otherwise, man could have been ruled through the general influx from Heaven without having Spirits and Angels adjoined to him.
, Explained.
To speak with Spirits is rarely granted (now), because it is dangerous; for the Spirits then know they are with a man... References.

Some who lead a solitary life sometimes hear Spirits... without danger; but the Spirits with them are removed... at intervals, to prevent their knowing they are with a man. For most Spirits do not know there is any other world... and therefore the man is not allowed to speak back to them, otherwise they would know.

They who think much about religious things, (so as) to see them in themselves, begin to hear Spirits speaking to them. Explained... But such are visionaries and enthusiasts, and whatever Spirit they bear they believe to be the Holy Spirit, when yet they are enthusiastic ones. Such Spirits see falsities as truths... and therefore they persuade those with whom they inflow. As these Spirits began to persuade evils also... they have been removed by degrees. (Continued. See
Rarely, since those times, has anyone spoken with Angels... but some with Spirits. Explained.
The Lord spoke the Word to the prophets through Spirits, whom He filled with His aspect. Explained.

A Spirit filled with the Divine... knows not but that he is the Lord, and that what he speaks is Divine... Afterwards, he perceives he is a Spirit... Such was the state of the Spirits who spoke to the prophets... The Spirits believed themselves to be Jehovah.
No Angel or Spirit is allowed to speak to a man from his own memory. (Fully quoted under

There are Spirits, called natural and corporeal Spirits, who, when they come to man, do not conjoin themselves with his thought, like other Spirits, but enter into his body, and take possession of all his senses, speak through his mouth, and act through his members, supposing, then, that all things of the man are theirs. These are the Spirits who obsess man; but they have been cast into Hell, and quite removed...
(The good and evil Spirits with man). Fully explained. See
All Spirits in the World of Spirits have communication with Heaven or with Hell. (Continued. See

The Spirits with man are changed according to the changes of his affections: hence some Spirits are with him in infancy; others in childhood; others in adolescence and young manhood, and others in old age. (These four classes of Spirits, and the Heavens with which they communicate. Described, Enumerated.)
As to his speech and actions, man is ruled through general influx, and therefore the Spirits adjoined to him have nothing in common with these.
The influx through Spirits is called mediate.
The Spirits with man (whether good or evil) never inflow from their own memory and derivative thought... Still, through them there inflows with man, good or evil affection. (Continued. See

Spirits not yet in conjunction with Hell (who) love undigested things... are present where there are such things in a man, and speak there together from their evil affection; and if this affection is contrary to the man's, it becomes in him sadness and melancholy anxiety; but if it is in agreement, it becomes in him gladness and cheerfulness. These Spirits appear near the stomach. Described.
Yet man cannot think one whit without Spirits adjoined to him; and his spiritual life depends upon it.
It is the spirit which thinks in the body.

For the spirit of man is altogether such as is his love; moreover, the body of every Spirit and Angel is the external form of his love exactly corresponding to the internal form which is that of his mind...
And that which is in the spirit of a man when he leaves the body remains after death; for he then lives a Spirit man.

Certain Spirits, not evil, fell as it were into sleep, and were translated, as to their interiors... into Heaven; (which) can be done with Spirits before their interiors have been opened. (What they saw, described.)
When, with a Spirit man, good has been conjoined with truth, he comes into Heaven... But when, with a Spirit man, evil has been conjoined with falsity, he comes into Hell.
When Spirits are mentioned, those who are in the World of Spirits are meant...
Every man is a Spirit as to his interiors. General article.
(Thus) whatever lives with man is his spirit.

It follows that the spirit is the man himself; or, that man, regarded in himself, is a Spirit, and is in a like form; for whatever lives and feels in man is of his spirit, and everything in man... lives and feels; and therefore when the body is separated from its spirit... the man remains a man, and is alive. Some think even in their cold body, while it is lying on the bier.
, Explained.

(Thus) the spirit of man is equally in a form... and equally enjoys sensories and senses when separated from the body; and everything... of the life of sense which man has, is not of his body, but of his spirit... Hence Spirits, equally with men, see, hear, and feel... The spirit sensates naturally while in the body, through what is material added to it; yet it sensates spiritually at the same time, by thinking and willing.
(Thus) man, regarded in himself, is a spirit; and the Corporeal which is added to him... is not the man; but is only the Instrumental of his spirit. (The Spiritual which beasts have. Explained.)
Every man, even while in the body, is as to his spirit in society with Spirits. Explained.
Being carried by the spirit into another place. Explained.

The inmost communication of the spirit is with the respiration and with the motion of the heart; its thought, with (the former), and its affection with (the latter); and therefore when these two motions cease, there is at once a separation... The spirit is then left to itself; and the body, being devoid of the life of its spirit, grows cold and putrescent.

The spirit remains a while in the body after the separation, but only until the total cessation of the heart, which takes place with variety according to the state of disease which was the cause of death. (Continued. See
(The drawing of the spirit out of the body. Explained.)
Man is man from his spirit. (Continued. See
The reason the spirit does not appear in its human form (before the natural sight). Explained.
Spirits (then) appear in their own form, not only the Spirits who are in the Spiritual World, but also the spirit (of a man), which, being in that World, is still in the body.
The reason the form of the spirit is the human one, is that man as to his spirit has been created after the form of Heaven. Explained.
That the spirit of man, after its solution from the body, is a man, and in a like form. From experience.

When the spirit of a man first enters the World of Spirits, which takes place shortly after his resuscitation, he has a like face and a like tone of voice, because he is then in the state of his exteriors... But afterwards his face becomes quite different; it becomes like his reigning love... in which his spirit had been in the body; for the face of a man's spirit is very different from that of his body, the latter being from his parents, whereas the face of his spirit is from his affection... Into this comes the spirit after (death) in the third state.
, Explained.

Recent Spirits I have Known from their face and speech; but not afterwards... For, regarded in himself, the spirit of a man is nothing but his own affection, the external of which is the face... Hence all who have Known each other (here). Know each other in the World of Spirits; but not in Heaven, nor in Hell.
That (Spirits) possess all sensation, memory, thought, affection... General article.

A Spirit man... sees, hears, speaks, etc. as before; he has appetite, longing and desire; thinks, reflects, is affected, loves, and wills, as before; and he who is delighted with studies, reads and writes as before. In a word, when a man passes from one life into the other... it is as if he had passed from one place to another; and he carries with him all things which he possesses in himself as a man...
Yet the difference between the life of man (as a Spirit) and his life here, is great. Explained.

Everything which a man has thought, willed, spoken, and done, and also which he has heard and seen, is inscribed... on his spirit, and on the members of its body; so that the spirit has been formed according to the thoughts and acts of its will. Fully explained.

When the spirit is in the Spiritual World, it does not think naturally, but spiritually. Hence the natural memory, as to material things, is then quiescent, and those things only come into use which the man has thereby imbibed and made rational. Explained.
Spirits and Angels have a memory equally with men. (Fully quoted under
All Spirits can be led wherever one pleases, provided they are kept in their reigning love. They cannot resist it. Explained.
A Spirit is his own reigning love. Explained.
Every man as to his spirit has exteriors and interiors. The exteriors of the spirit are... The interiors of the spirit are...
The life of recent Spirits. Described.
The Spirit man is then let into the state of his interiors. Explained.
Therefore, when the Spirit man is in this state, he is in himself...
, Explained.
, Explained.
, Explained.
For Spirits not only think, but also speak, from their own affection.
For the memory of Spirits is in their life... For Spirits are affections, and are in a human form like their affections.
After Spirits have been prepared for Heaven by instructions... they are clothed in angelic garments...
For men are ruled... through Spirits who are in the World of Spirits.
(Thus) the Lord draws away every Spirit to Himself through Angels, and also through influx from Heaven; but Spirits who are in evil resist...
He is then no longer a Spirit man, as he was in his first state; but is truly a Spirit, (that is) he has a face and body which correspond to his internals. Described.
The excellence of Spirits in comparison with men. Explained.

The spirit of a man, while he lives (here) is bound to the body, and through it is in the natural world, and therefore what it then thinks spiritually inflows into natural ideas... But when the spirit is loosed from the body, and comes into its spiritual state... its state as to thoughts and affections immensely excels its former one.
For the spirit of man, when loosed from the body, is in its own good, or evil. Explained.
An Angel or Spirit cannot see anything in the natural world...
Spirits who avert themselves become invisible.
What is not of the love or will of a man is not of his spirit; for the esse of the spirit of a man is love or will.

The conjunction of man with Heaven and with Hell is not immediately with them, but mediately through Spirits who are in the World of Spirits. These Spirits are with man, and none from Hell itself, or Heaven itself.
The Spirits adjoined to man are Subjects. Explained.
The simple have an innate idea that a Spirit is a man.
(References on the subject of the Spirits through whom communications are effected.)
The will and understanding make the spirit of man... The body is only obedience.
An internal merely natural man... is a Spirit, and not an Angel; and, while he lives in the body, is in society with Spirits, but with those in Hell.
For that only remains in the spirit of a man which has entered into his love. After death all other things are regarded as alien.

Angels and Spirits are with man, and in his affections... but they do not know with what men they are; as neither do the men know with what Angels and Spirits they cohabit. The Lord alone knows and disposes this...
So when a man... dies, then, being a Spirit, he does not subsist upon his own proper basis; but upon the general basis, which is the human race.
No Angel or Spirit can subsist without man; and no man without a Spirit and Angel. The conjunction is mutual and reciprocal.
A Spirit in his first state does not know that (he is bound to a Society)... While he is such, he goes hither and thither... and he appears in many other places. (Continued. See
For the spirit of man... is formed from his will, and from his thought in so far as it proceeds from his will.

The cunning (of the Babylonians) is more malignant there, because they are spirits; and all wickedness stores itself up in the spirit; for the spirit of man is what thinks, wills, intends, and machinates.
Thus they do these things in spirit.
All Spirits and Angels are from the human race.
The quality of any Spirit manifests itself there by influx, which is the communication of his affection. Described.
Spirits and Angels rarely come to the men of Jupiter after they are thirty years old, because they then no longer suffer themselves to be led by them.
Spirits also perceive the Word in its internal sense in so far as their interiors are open into Heaven.
They then receive the idea that the Holy Spirit is the presence of the Lord with man through Angels and Spirits.
, Explained.
That by
spirit
is meant the life of man. Explained.
. Illustrated.

The life of man is various according to its state, and therefore by
spirit
is meant the various affection of the life with man. Enumerated, Illustrated.
(By

are also meant) the infernal spirits themselves. Illustrated.
By

By

Where

is mentioned in relation to the Lord, His Divine life is meant, thus the Lord Himself. Illustrated.
By
spirit,
where the Lord is treated of, is meant in special the life of His wisdom, which is Divine Truth. Illustrated.
When the prophets were in vision, they were not in their body, but in their spirit. Illustrated.
(Thus) in the Word alone... there is spirit and life. Illustrated.
That Angels and Spirits are men like men here... with the sole difference that they are spiritual...
God

= life from the Lord.

= to respire no longer.
They are spirit and they are life
= (the Divine wisdom and the Divine love).
As to the interiors of his mind, every man is a spirit.

Angels and Spirits are in a totally different light and heat from men... They are not within nature, but entirely above or outside it, and in their own world... They are together with man, conjoined with the affection and thought of his spirit. For man is a Spirit; from this he thinks and wills: and therefore the Spiritual World is where man is, (who) as to the interiors of his mind is in the midst of Angels and Spirits.
As to his spirit, man is in a certain quarter of the Spiritual World.
For, as to his mind, man is a spirit; and, if he is in love and wisdom, he is an Angel; and therefore after death... he becomes a Spirit or an Angel.
Every Spirit turns himself to his reigning love. Explained.
So long as he stays in the World of Spirits, he is called a Spirit...
All the Spirits in the World of Spirits are adjoined to men...
The Spirits below the Heavens appear as if in a cloud
Hence it is that there is no Spirit or Angel who was not born a man.
Such is the state of Spirits and Angels, who are men, even as to their bodies: they appear in the place where their thought is.
No one can think unless the pulmonary spirit (or breath) concurs and accords. Explained... If he hold his breath, he cannot think, except in his spirit, from its respiration.
The mind of man is his spirit, and the spirit a man; the body being the external through which the mind or spirit sensates and acts in its world. General article.
(Origin of the human form of the spirit.)

The conjunction of the spirit with the body is through the correspondence of its will and understanding with its heart and lungs; and the disjunction is through their non-correspondence. General article.
The spirit (also) has a pulse and respiration, (which) inflow into those of the body, and produce them.
The spirit then goes away and continues its life in the Spiritual World.

When questioned, Spirits and Angels have said that they are as much men as men in the world; that they have a body, and feel the beating of the heart in the breast, and of the arteries on the palm, just as well.
That the spirit of man respires in his body, shown by experience.
I have sometimes been reduced to the respiration of my spirit alone...
Then I was in the spirit, outside the body...
When a man is alone, he thinks from his spirit.
Man is in manifest thought when his spirit thinks in the body... But when he is in the affection of understanding... he is in the thought of his spirit...
The respiration of the spirit depends on fibres from the brains; that of the body on the blood vessels...
As Angels and Spirits are affections... and thoughts... they are not in space and time; but only in the appearance of them...
Hence it is that with every man there are spirits present who are in like affection... and they are as really present as if the man were included in their Society.
Spirits and Angels are affections and derivative thoughts.

Every spirit of a man is affection and the derivative thought; (therefore) every spirit is his own love and thence his own understanding; (so that) when a man is thinking solely from his own spirit... he thinks from the affection of his love; (and it follows) that when a man becomes a Spirit... he is the affection of his own love... And as all Spirits and Angels are affections, it is evident that the universal Heaven is the love of all affections of good, and the derivative wisdom of all perceptions of truth.
So also can one Spirit be infilled by another, even until he knows not but that he is the other.
They still do the evils in their spirit: for it is the spirit of man which thinks and wills.

As it is the spirit of man which wills and understands... it follows that this external and internal of thought are the external and internal of the spirit of man. What the body does is only an effect from the internal and external of his spirit; for the body is only obedience.

For the internal of man's thought, or his internal man, is his spirit itself; and in it are things more infinite and innumerable than there are in his body; for the spirit of man is man in his own form; and all things of it correspond to all things of man in his body.

So neither does man know how the Lord operates into all things of his mind or soul, that is, into all things of his spirit... But still the Lord cannot purify man from any concupiscence... in his spirit or internal man so long as the man keeps the external closed... by evils.
Hence it is that the spirit of man

For the mind of man is his spirit; and, according to the conjunction with the Lord, it is an Angel; and the body is obedience.
Visions induced by enthusiastic Spirits, and visionary ones...
a. 2. Speech with the dead would produce an effect like that of miracles... But this happens only when the Spirits bring in something dogmatic of religion, which is never done by any good Spirit...
Still, speech with Spirits is possible, but rarely with Angels. (Continued. See
.) They never teach.
Like one with his breath held.
Hence it is that no Angel or Spirit was created immediately; but all were first born men.
The spirit (of an infernal) is itself an evil...
. It is inhaled with full breath.
Man's mind is his spirit which lives after death, (which) is in the whole form in which is Heaven, or Hell: there is no difference, except that one is the greatest, and the other the least...
For man as to his spirit is in the Spiritual World, and in some Society there, (Continued. See

One Spirit can infuse his thoughts and affections into another Spirit, and the latter know no otherwise than that what is infused is of his Own thought and affection. This is called thinking from another, and thinking in another. I have seen it a thousand times, and have done it a hundred; and yet the appearance of distance was great. But as soon as they knew it was another... they were indignant, and averted themselves... Evil Spirits have often injected into my thought evils and falsities... and I have inquired who injected them... and they were at a great distance from me.
It is the mind or spirit which (sensates in the body)... But still the mind or spirit of man does not sensate of itself, but from the Lord.
Those instructed by influx what to believe and do, are not instructed by the Lord, nor by any Angel; but by some enthusiastic Spirit, Quaker, or Moravian, and are led astray.
By this, spirit comes into his civil and moral things, and they live; otherwise, there is no spirit in them...
He then becomes a Spirit in human form: his mind is that Spirit.
The spirit of man cannot be anywhere else than in the delight of his life, because this makes its life, and even its very respiration and the pulsation of its heart. It is otherwise (here).

) = all in Divine truth; in the abstract sense, the Divine Truth itself. ( = the Divine in Heaven.

Distant Spirits hear better when I think tacitly.
That Spirits also sleep.
That my representations are seen by Spirits as it were alive.
Spirits seem to themselves to inhabit well-furnished houses... according to the genius of each one; and thus are bent to good...
Some Spirits do not want such things, but money. I told them that they do not need to buy anything there. Explained.
Certain from the families of Spirits thought...
The Spirits around man are such that as soon as any truth comes forth... they feel a repugnance.
They take with them there a high spirit (and want to be greater than others).
On the interior thought of Spirits.
They thus become interior Spirits.
On interior Spirits.
, Explained.
, Explained.
The difference between exterior and interior Spirits.
After some delay. Spirits are brought by the Lord into this interior state, as it were through sleep...
Spirits have often wondered that they were in the other life...

If men were in faith in the Lord, Heaven could be thus opened to them... almost as in me, and thus there would be an intercourse of Souls, Spirits, and Angels with men in the world... so that Spirits would know what is going on in the world, and men what is going on in Heaven. Thus they would live together, both ways. (It has been ordained by the Lord from eternity that there should be such an intercourse.

I told the Spirits that they are not near me, although they seem to be... so near as to touch me... It is a most certain experience that they cannot be here, but sometimes 10, 100, 1000, 3000 miles distant... But the Spirits did not want to believe it... See
The Spirits said they do not know they have such superior faculties...
et seq
. Spirits thrown down upon me, having been ejected from the society of Angels for being in a false idea.
That Spirits perceive quite fully the thoughts of man.
That Spirits, too, are at once carried into doing evil when the reins are slackened.

The Spirits (of the interior sphere) do indeed inflow into the thoughts of man, but do not perceive them; but only his intentions; and therefore when such (evil) intentions are absent, they cannot understand; and then good Spirits take them up, who are also interior Spirits...
These interior Spirits cannot be where there are good interior Spirits, just as they cannot be together in this world. Explained.
The Spirits in the interior sphere use the Spirits in the exterior sphere...

In the life of the body, although the Spirits are distinct, they appear to them to be a one... (and thus) they put on the man himself, because such Spirits are with him as suppose themselves to be the man.
That there is a great multitude of Spirits who take delight in inflicting injury on others.
That Spirits know from reflection that they are present.
How the first man existed without Spirits and Angels.
So with Spirits: although myriads concur to one idea, or word, each one supposes that he alone does it.

That Spirits who are of the same genus and species can be induced to believe that they are the same... And they induce other Spirits to believe they are the same... Such Spirits have been with me, and have wanted to persuade me, because they themselves were persuaded, that they were those same persons.

Therefore let those to whom it is granted to speak with Spirits beware of believing that they are those whom they say they are... for those who are like in genus and species... conduct themselves in the same way... (Moreover) such Spirits are in general associated with those who are like him, and, while with him, they know no otherwise than that they are the same.
An idea of interior Spirits is inexpressible; yet is intelligible to those who are separated from the world while they live in the body...
The speech, ideas, and felicities (of the Angels) are the continual beginnings of those of the interior Spirits; and, through this, of those of the lower Spirits, or of men.
Spirits who are wizards and witches: they spoke with others as if it were I.
They are proud of being subtle, and within the sphere of speech... in which are the interior Spirits...
But a Spirit cannot be dissolved and perish.
So that no Spirit may lose anything of what belongs to his natural mind and memory.
On the speech of the Spirits of the interior sphere.
Spirits who can induce others to believe whatever they like.
Although Spirits do not see natural objects, a certain sense comes from them to them. Explained.
A Spirit who had committed a crime, and caused the surrounding Spirits to believe themselves guilty of it.
Such persuasions have the effect that they cannot be with other Spirits.
How the speech of man is ruled through Spirits.
On the quality of the Spirits who at this day come from the world.
Such need more Spirits; those who are led according to order, fewer.
The operations of the internal viscera do not need the immediate aid of Spirits, because they are according to order.
That Spirits see all the thoughts of man, and what he has thought, and his intentions, and yet do not know that they are not the men.

Every Spirit takes out of the memory that which belongs to his own nature; and thus man is rent, suffers, ... just as unclean Spirits have seen things I have not seen myself, and have directed my eyes to filthy things... of which I must have remained wholly ignorant, unless such Spirits had known, felt, and thus seen them. The reason is, that they remove, and thus do not see, all things which do not accord with their unclean delights.
On traveller Spirits, whom other Spirits flee from: they make a sound as of little bells.
Persecution by interior Spirits...
That Spirits are found and affected by my looks
On the other hand, Spirits, by their looks into me, take out of my memory...
On the bodies of Spirits.
The Spirits associated with man.
Spirits appropriate all the knowledges of man... Whatever a man is skilled in, the Spirits possess as their own. Example(s).
These stationary Spirits kept me half way between sleep and waking...
These Spirits supposed they were living in the body.
That Spirits cannot assail persuasions with man; they are as it were in the like persuasion...
That some Spirits do not at once put on the memory of man.
That the interior Spirits have a subtle perception...
When permitted, Spirits can, unknown to me, take many things from my memory.
With what difficulty man can be persuaded that he is ruled through Spirits.
That Spirits converse together exactly as men do.

When I was in a shop, the Spirits infused a desire that I should buy this or That... which I did not perceive; for, as is my wont in company, I was devoid of reflection upon Spirits. It was then given to the Spirits to reflect upon their state, in that they had caused me to buy (something) and change it; and they said that it was exactly as if they had done it... So that Spirits have a life with men exactly as if they were the man...
That Spirits have no power, and yet their life is happy.
It has often happened that when anyone has spoken to me. Spirits have spoken (and laughed) through me. Described.
That the style of my writing is varied according to the Spirits associated with me.
On the bonds in which Spirits are held.
That Spirits do not speak from themselves.
. (See
How and wherefore Spirits suppose that they think from themselves, and are not kept in bonds.
That if Spirits enjoyed the corporeal memory, they could not be in a spiritual state.
On Spirits who want to be believed to be the Lord.
That Spirits have no life unless they are allowed the things they desire.
That some Spirits exceedingly desire to be men, and to occupy their bodies.
How the influx of Spirits takes place into man.

Man is the ultimate of order... and all ideas, even those of Spirits, are terminated in man's memory... A Spirit cannot but think that his ideas begin in himself... when yet his ideas are in the ideas of the man in which they are terminated, as may be evident from the fact that they appropriate to themselves each and all things of the man...
Each kind of Spirit seizes in an idea that which accords with themselves...

a. The more that ideas are closed by man... the less can Spirits infuse into him evils in addition to what he has already acquired. But with him who is in faith, the less his ideas are determined to one thing, the better it is. Explained.
In speech with Spirits the idea in a word is most exquisitely observed. Example(s).
On the true speech of Spirits.
On some Spirits who supposed it to be a phantasy that I have conversed with Spirits, and that there are any Spirits.
The effect on Spirits of the phantasies of others. Described.
a. How dangerous it is for any learned person who is imbued with phantasies to speak with Spirits.
That the quality of a Spirit may be Known from a single word.
That one Spirit is led by another into almost the like thoughts.
Spirits suppose they can carry off the things they see. Example(s).
(Evil Spirits, although shown that they are Spirits, at once forget it; but good Spirits have reflection given them, so that they continue to know it.)
, Example(s).

The first cause why a Spirit supposes himself to be a man, is that no reflection is given him while he is with a man who does not speak to him, or answer him; for speaking with a Spirit is conjoined with their reflecting upon him who speaks; thus that they are not man, but separate from man, and thus Spirits.

(Another reason) is that the Spirit puts on the man's memory, thus he puts on the man... But they do not possess the interior memory; this is possessed by the Angels who rule the Spirits who are below... When a man reaches the point that his interior memory is ruled by the interior Spirits
the
man
can
live
no
longer.
Spirits suppose that they could have been led differently and thus have become better...
That the bodies of Spirits are beheld in a fixed attitude as well as in a fixed place.
On speech with Spirits. (See
Therefore Spirits are in a more perfect state...
That Spirits speak those things which others think interiorly.
That Spirits retain in the interior memory the things they hear, see, and perceive... but they cannot recall them; the Lord alone can.
How it is that a Spirit seems to lose everything of his own.
That a Spirit supposed himself to be completely me, and that he was endowed with a body.

When I stretched out my hand, another spirit supposed... that he took hold of it... And when other Spirits insisted that they were as it were my body, I told them that my body is adjoined to my spirit, so that it is the body of my spirit, and that the bodies of their spirits are dead; so that they inflowed only into my spirit, as one Spirit does into another; and that when my spirit acts with my body, they suppose that they act with my body; but it is impossible for another spirit to possess another body, except by acting as one obsessed; for no spirit squares with my body except my own... There is a connection of my spirit with my body which can never exist between another spirit and my body.
